   - Implementation evidence: `prepareQuery` rejects the window with `if (windowSpan(query) > AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow) throw new Error('audit query window is too long');` (`src/audit/audit-query.mjs:9`). `windowSpan` returns a value in minutes: `export const windowSpan = (window) => (window.until - window.from) / MINUTE;` (`src/audit/retention.mjs:13`), while `AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow` is a millisecond duration: `maxQueryWindow: minutes(10_080)` (`src/audit/retention.mjs:5`), and `minutes(count) => count * MINUTE` with `MINUTE = 60_000` (`src/platform/time.mjs:1-3`).
   - Governing requirement: "An audit query has integer `from` and `until`, `until` later than `from` by at most 10080 minutes, and a `limit` that is an integer from 1 to 500, or 500 when absent (undefined or null)." (governing-spec.md, "Audit trail")
   - Problem and impact: the comparison divides by `MINUTE` on one side and multiplies by `MINUTE` on the other, so the effective ceiling is 604800000 minutes (about 1149 years) instead of 10080 minutes.    - Fix: compare in one unit. Either keep `maxQueryWindow` in minutes (`maxQueryWindow: 10_080`) so `windowSpan(query) > AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow` is a minutes-to-minutes comparison, or compare the raw span: `query.until - query.from > AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow`.

hasEnded compares minutesBetween(at, endAt), whole minutes truncated toward zero, with 0, so a closure with less than one minute left (for example 30 seconds) counts as ended: adding it is rejected and it is left out of the upcoming closures.
